question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist for Slack message sends now, and should that policy be Slack-specific channel config or part of a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding `allowTo` changes public config and outbound authorization semantics under a documented trusted-operator model, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
options.body: Add a documented allowTo-style recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement at the shared outbound/channel send boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track this as a Slack recipient-authorization acceptance case under #87870 so sanitizer, verified delivery, and target authorization are designed together.

options.title: Decline core allowTo for now
options.body: Keep the trusted-operator model and document that `dmPolicy` and `allowFrom` do not constrain explicit operator sends.

recommendation.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented allowTo-style recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement at the shared outbound/channel send boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across message-tool introduction, outbound helper ownership, Slack allowFrom config lineage, and prior trusted-operator triage.
